description_en: Khapiṁchẽ Phalcā is a five-bayedphalcāthat faces into the courtyard it stands in. An additional bay contains a Nārāyaṇa shrine that opens up westwards to the public path. The courtyard is also home to an Ākāśabhairava temple, anotherphalcā(LAL4132) and acāpaḥ. The building was severly affected by the 2015 earthquake. Prior to this, it was already dismantled and reconstructed in 2012, when veneer bricks and new woodwork were added to the structure. Until then, the shrine facing the road and the Phalcā had been made up of two independent buildings.A terracotta pinnacle can be seen upon the roof of the Phalcā; it is located just above the northern corner of the building, above a shrine containing a statue of Viṣṇu. Two terracotta statues of lions have been placed to the right and left of the pinnacle. One of the lions is damaged. Normally, lion statues can be found on the left and right sides of the entrance to a shrine or a temple, making their placement here somewhat unusual.The Phalca is situated in in a small but lively locality. The first floor is currently used by the Tol Suddhar Samiti. Dāphā Bhajana performances take place here during the whole month of Kārttika.
description_ne: खपिंछेँ फल्चामा चोकतर्फ फर्केका पाँचवटा कवल र नारायणको देवल रहेको पश्चिमपट्टि फर्केको एउटा कवल रहेको छ । यस फल्चाको पछाडिपट्टि अकाशभैरव मन्दिर, अर्को एउटा फल्चा र चपाः रहेका छन् । सानो तर सजीव सामाजिक परिवेश भएको यस एरियाका घरहरू सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पका कारण निकै क्षतिग्रस्त भए । सन् २०१२ मा यो फल्चा भत्काएर नयाँ इँटा र काठ प्रयोग गरी पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो । फल्चाको पहिलो तलामा टोल सुधार समितिको कार्यालय रहेको छ । कार्त्तिक महिनाभरि यस फल्चामा दाफा भजन हुने गर्दछ । फल्चाको उत्तरतर्फको कुनामा रहेको विष्णुको मूर्तिको ठीक माथि पर्ने गरी फल्चाको छानामा पाको माटोको गजूर राखिएको छ ।  गजूरको दायाँ-बायाँ पाको माटोकै सिंहका मूर्ति राखिएका छन्, तीमध्ये एउटा मूर्ति फुटेको छ । सामान्यतया सिंहका मूर्ति कुनै पनि देवस्थलको अगाडि राख्ने गरेको पाइन्छ तर यहाँ भने फल्चाको गजुरको दायाँ-बायाँ ती मूर्ति राखेको पाइन्छ ।
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired), Rebuilt

historical_events.event_description: Construction of the Phalcāwith the support of the Bhāvo and Prajāpati communities of the Khapiṁchẽ area. A stone inscription attached to the eastern wall provides further information about its construction, which took place in 1840.
This reconstruction led to the addition of another storey and the inclusion of the shrine into the building.
